description: Statically derived by reading app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl, never captured from a run: the COBOL cannot be executed in this environment. EIBCALEN is 0, so the guard at :388-401 INITIALIZEs CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA and sets CDEMO-PGM-ENTER with CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, the AID stays ENTER through the coercion at :413-424, and the ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :429 passes over arm one (:435-439, PF03 and the two done/failed arms) and arm two (:482-485, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equal to LIT-CCLISTPGM) before matching arm three at :502-503, which performs 3000-SEND-MAP THRU 3000-SEND-MAP-EXIT at :507-508, flips the context to REENTER at :509 and leaves through COMMON-RETURN at :511. Every sent value is read from source at the width app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY declares for its xxxI item (4/40/8/8/40/8/11/16/50/1/2/4/2/40/80/21/18): 3100 fills CCRDUPAO with LOW-VALUES at :1053 before moving the two active COTTL01Y titles, LIT-THISTRANID and LIT-THISPGM, and the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS renderings of the pinned clock; 3200 CONTINUEs at :1084-1085 under CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, so the seven data items keep those LOW-VALUES; 3250's first arm at :1141 supplies the X(40) prompt while WS-RETURN-MSG is still SPACES from :384, leaving ERRMSGO blank at its X(80) width; and 3300 marks and reddens nothing, because :1248's CDEMO-PGM-REENTER guard and the CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK guards from :1264 onward are all false - this case is the ENTER half of gate G38. Only EXPDAYC differs from DFHDFCOL, from the unconditional MOVE DFHBMDAR at :1285, and FKEYSO and FKEYSCO stay LOW-VALUES because the program never writes them - their text is a physical-map INITIAL in app/bms/COCRDUP.bms:162 and :167 that CICS merges at send time. Nothing is written on this path, so expectedWrites is empty by design rather than by omission; CARDDAT is seeded from the first three rows of fixtures/carddata.txt (row 1 is card 0500024453765740, account 00000000050, at the 150-byte CVACT02Y width) only because the handler is reached with a card key, and the cold start reads no record at all.
